justification: Assessment returned INVALID and localized the failure to step 0012, the induction step of the Bellman-Ford loop invariant, stating that the claimed equality dist[u] = min length over <=k-edge paths fails because in-place relaxation lets dist[v] be updated earlier in the same iteration, so dist[u] can be strictly smaller than OPT_k(u). That is precisely the ground-truth flaw. Its witness is different but valid: on s->a (1), a->b (-5), s->b (10) with scan order (s,a),(a,b),(s,b), iteration 1 gives dist[a]=1, then dist[b]=min(inf,1-5)=-4, then min(-4,10)=-4; the only <=1-edge s-b path is s->b of length 10, so dist[b]=-4 < 10=OPT_1(b), violating the equality in the same direction as the ground truth. Verified the trace by hand; the graph is a DAG so no negative-cycle objection applies. Same defect, valid alternate witness.
